userEnteredValue.stringValue:
Who vs. Whose

Design starts with identity. Before we explore your gifts, personality, or purpose, we need to begin with something more foundational: who you belong to.

“Who am I?” is an important question. But in discovering your divine design, it finds its deepest meaning when grounded in another question: “Whose am I?”

Who Are You?
When you describe yourself, you might talk about:
• Your personality
• Your experiences
• Your talents
• Your story
• How others describe you

These things matter. They help you recognize what makes you unique and how you engage with the world. Your experiences have shaped your perspective. Your talents influence what comes naturally. Your personality affects how you connect, contribute, and respond.

But none of these can carry the full weight of your identity. Your abilities can change. Your roles can shift. Other people’s opinions can be mistaken. Even your own understanding of yourself can be shaped by disappointment, comparison, or past mistakes. If these become the foundation of your identity, your sense of worth can rise and fall with how well life is going.

Whose You Are?
For those who belong to Jesus, there is a deeper foundation:
• You are a child of God.
• You are fully known.
• You are deeply loved.
• You are secure in Christ.
• You belong to the One who created you.

“Whose you are” is about belonging before achievement. You do not have to discover your gifts, prove your usefulness, or figure out your purpose to become worthy of God’s love.

“See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!” — 1 John 3:1 (NIV)

Your relationship with God is not another item on the list of things that describe you. It is the foundation from which you begin to understand everything else.

Why This Matters for Your Design
When you start with “who,” discovering your design can become a search for proof that you matter. You may compare your gifts with someone else’s, wish you had a different personality, or feel that your story disqualifies you. When you start with “whose,” you can approach discovery from a place of belonging. You are not trying to earn your place in God’s family. You are learning how to live as someone who already belongs to Him.

Who you are may describe you. Whose you are defines you.

userEnteredValue.stringValue:
Connect
Pause and think: When you hear “You are a child of God,” how does your heart respond? Does it feel true, or do old labels and doubts rise up? 
When you hear 'You are a child of God,' how does your heart respond?

Act
Name one lie or label and place it beside a Scripture-rooted truth. Tape it somewhere you’ll see it daily.
Write one lie or label you have believed, then write the truth God says about you.

Reflect
Ask whether your identity is shaped more by who you think you are or by whose you are.
Is your identity shaped more by who you think you are or by whose you are?

Explore
Imagine how tomorrow changes when you focus on whose you are. 
How might your life be different tomorrow if you focused on whose rather than who?

Prayer
“Jesus, help me let go of the names I’ve given myself or that others have put on me. Show me how to see myself the way You do: as beloved, chosen, and made new. Help me walk in the truth of whose I am so I can live in the peace You offer. Jesus, quiet the voices that tell me I’m anything less than Yours. When I’m tempted to wear old labels or live from old wounds, remind me who I truly am in You. Help me to rest in Your love, to believe I am fully accepted, fully forgiven, and fully known. Shape my identity by Your truth, and teach me to live as Your beloved child today.”
